title: Nimbadesk help-desk product one-pagers: neutralize eight mixed-light product-screen photos to an in-frame grey card as one brand family, prep-and-vectorize the wordmark, and data-merge one press-ready sell sheet per module

source.reference: Marketing Collateral & Brand Assets (One-Page Service Overview / Sell Sheet)

grounding_note: VERBATIM from the source Upwork brief: "DELIVERABLE 2 - One-Page Service Overview: single/double-sided 8.5\"x11\" sell sheet"; "header with branding and compelling title"; a "\"company advantage\" section"; "core-services bullets"; "a prominent CTA"; "clean grids, profess[ional]" layout; overall deliverables "must feel clean, modern, trustworthy and polished, referencing the website's palette/typography." The original brief's legal/MVA case-management firm is laundered to a fictional, IP-clean B2B SaaS company ("Nimbadesk", a coined nimbus+desk portmanteau, distinct from any real help-desk mark). REASONABLY ENRICHED and REPAIRED against two audits into a runnable Adobe-connector benchmark. (audit 1 - broken merge path) The prior version ran convert_pdf_to_indd and merged into the converted PDF - fields will NOT bind that way, and it is a BANNED merge target; and its CSV carried no image column, so the graded screenshots and the vector logo had no route into the layout and the sheets would print with empty frames. Both are fixed the AO-74 way: the client supplies a genuinely hand-authored single-record InDesign template (.indd, NOT a converted PDF) carrying live <<fields>> plus TWO @-prefixed image-path columns (@hero for that module's prepped product-screen photo and @wordmark for the shared vectorized wordmark), so both agent-produced assets reach every sheet as a MERGE BIND, never free-form placement; convert_pdf_to_indd is gone. (audit 2 - consistency asserted, not measurable; batch amputated) The prior version graded three screenshots with canned auto_tone + a canned monochromatic_tint and asserted they 'feel like one family' with no measurable target and no failure the grader could catch. Repositioned so the sell-sheet SET covers the Nimbadesk help-desk PRODUCT SUITE - one one-pager per module (eight modules) - which turns the merge into a genuine per-row batch AND restores a cross-asset grade of EIGHT differently-lit assets. The eight heroes are now real camera captures of each module shown on a device on a real desk under deliberately mismatched light (warm lamp, cool window, green fluorescent, mixed, over-exposed), each carrying a photographic 18% grey card in frame so 'one brand family' becomes a checkable neutralisation target the agent drives BY EYE and REPORTS (never a pixel readout). The house look is now agent-AUTHORED from primitives (a split-tone + tone move via image_apply_adjustments applied as shared constants) rather than a preset or auto_tone, and the deprecated image_adjust_color_temperature / image_adjust_brightness_and_contrast / image_apply_auto_tone calls are replaced by image_apply_adjustments. No deliverable is invented beyond the per-module sell sheets the brief asks for; from-scratch layout is NOT in connector scope so the authored template is a supplied input.
one_line_ask: Bring eight mixed-lighting product-screen photos of the Nimbadesk help-desk suite to one consistent brand look by neutralising each to the 18% grey card it carries, decide per frame how far to move white balance and exposure without wrecking any screen's intended design, prep and vectorize the scanned wordmark, then data-merge the client's authored single-record InDesign template against the module roster to produce one press-ready sell sheet per module plus a high-res JPEG.
full_brief: Nimbadesk sells a B2B customer-support help-desk platform and needs a product one-pager per module for the sales team's leave-behind binder - one clean US-Letter (8.5" x 11" portrait) sell sheet per module in the suite, each carrying the module name, a tagline, a short summary, three core-feature bullets, a price line and a 'Book a demo' CTA, with a hero image of that module's screen at the top and the Nimbadesk wordmark crisp in the header. Our production designer has already hand-built the InDesign layout: a single-record sell-sheet template on a clean modern grid with real InDesign data-merge fields (<<module_name>>, <<tagline>>, <<summary>>, <<feature_1>>, <<feature_2>>, <<feature_3>>, <<price_line>>, <<cta_line>>) plus TWO image frames wired to merge columns - a hero frame bound to @hero and a header frame bound to @wordmark. This is a production/finishing job, NOT a fresh branding exercise. We will hand off: the authored .indd, a brand kit (deep navy #0E1F3D, signal blue #3B82F6, fog-grey #F5F7FA, typography notes), a roster CSV with one row per module (Shared Inbox, Live Chat, Insights, Flow Builder, Knowledge Base, Voice Callback, SLA Manager, Customer Portal) carrying the copy verbatim, the wordmark as a flat scan on off-white paper, and eight hero photos - and here is the problem with the photos. Marketing shot each module running on a laptop or monitor on a real desk, over two afternoons in different rooms, so straight out of the folder they do NOT match: some sit under warm desk-lamp light, some against a cool window, one under old green fluorescents, one is a mixed split, one came out over-exposed by a sunny window; a couple are a little tilted. To make the set checkable we clipped a photographic 18% grey card into the corner of every shot. Your job on the photos: bring every image to a consistent, on-brand look by neutralising each one to the grey card it contains - the card must read as a clean neutral grey (equal across the channels) in your finished frame, and once every card is neutral the whole set shares one white point and the eight sheets look like one product suite, not eight snapshots. Then carry ONE shared, restrained house look across all eight (a subtle split-tone that leans the shadows gently toward our navy and keeps highlights clean, modest contrast and clarity) so the set feels deliberately designed - but do NOT force one blanket white-balance across the batch: each photo was lit differently and needs its own decision to land on the shared target. When you are done, tell us the white-balance and exposure move you settled on for each frame so we can confirm they were matched, not eyeballed. Be careful with two of them. One module (Insights) is a genuinely DARK-themed UI by design - it is supposed to look dark; its grey card was shot under neutral light and already reads neutral, so drive its exposure by the card only and do NOT brighten the frame trying to 'rescue' the dark screen or you will destroy the intended look and push its card off the set. And one module (Flow Builder) was captured before our brand refresh, so its in-app accent buttons are still the OLD teal instead of our signal blue - bring just those action buttons to signal blue with the button sheen and label intact, without tinting the rest of the neutral chrome; the other seven already show the new blue and must be left alone. Second, the wordmark only exists as a flat scan on off-white paper - get it clean, square and razor-sharp as a vector for the sheet header so it does not print like a fuzzy scan. Finally build the sheets: merge the roster against the authored template so every module gets its own single-page sheet with its copy bound, its matching prepped screen photo dropped into the hero frame, and the crisp vector wordmark dropped into the header, then hand back one press-ready ~300 DPI US-Letter PDF covering every module (one page per module) and a high-resolution JPEG of the same set for email. Keep everything on the supplied palette and bind the copy verbatim from the roster - do not rewrite it.

inputs.name: nimbadesk_sellsheet_template.indd
inputs.gen_prompt: AUTHORED DELIVERABLE (cannot be model-generated): a genuine, hand-built Adobe InDesign document (.indd/.idml) for a SINGLE-RECORD US-Letter (8.5" x 11", portrait) B2B SaaS product sell sheet on a clean modern grid. It must contain live InDesign data-merge placeholder fields <<module_name>>, <<tagline>>, <<summary>>, <<feature_1>>, <<feature_2>>, <<feature_3>>, <<price_line>>, <<cta_line>> arranged into a branded header, a 'Why teams switch to Nimbadesk' company-advantage block, a three-bullet core-features list and a prominent 'Book a demo' CTA band, PLUS TWO @-prefixed image-path merge columns wired to two separate image frames: a hero image frame near the top bound to @hero (the module's prepped product-screen photo) and a header logo frame bound to @wordmark (the vectorized wordmark). Because free-form image-at-coordinates placement is banned, BOTH the hero photo and the wordmark reach the page ONLY as merge binds through these two image frames - never dropped in by hand. Uses the brand palette (#0E1F3D navy, #3B82F6 signal blue, #F5F7FA fog-grey). Built by hand in InDesign so the merge fields and BOTH image fields actually bind; explicitly NOT a convert_pdf_to_indd output (a converted-PDF template with literal typed text would not bind) and NOT a multi-record grid (document_merge_data_layout emits one file per row, so the template holds exactly one record's worth of fields).
inputs.realism_notes: document_merge_data_layout is [T] and REQUIRES a user-authored .indd carrying real merge fields plus genuine @image-path columns, and it produces ONE FILE PER ROW - so a single-record sell sheet is the correct, connector-doable shape. Supplied as an input, not a chain output; a PDF-converted .indd would not bind. TWO image columns (@hero, @wordmark) give BOTH the agent-produced hero photo AND the agent-produced vector wordmark a real, connector-doable path onto every sheet without any free-form placement (mirrors AO-74's @image/@Wordmark pattern). This is the fix for the prior version's convert_pdf_to_indd merge target and its image-less CSV.

inputs.name: nimbadesk_brand_kit.pdf
inputs.gen_prompt: Generate a concise one-page brand-kit reference PDF for a fictional B2B SaaS brand 'Nimbadesk': primary palette deep navy #0E1F3D, signal blue #3B82F6, fog-grey #F5F7FA; heading font is a geometric sans; body font TBD (to be recommended); wordmark clear-space and minimum-size rules; the in-app accent colour is signal blue #3B82F6 as of the current brand refresh (older captures may still show a legacy teal accent that should be brought to signal blue); tone = clean, modern, trustworthy. Note the sell sheets must reference this palette/typography.
inputs.realism_notes: Stands in for the brief's 'referencing the website's palette/typography'; establishes the navy-leaning split-tone the agent authors as the shared house look and the signal-blue in-app accent target for the one drifted capture. IP-clean fictional brand. Does NOT tell the agent WHICH capture is the drifted one - that is discovered by opening the frames.

inputs.name: nimbadesk_modules.csv
inputs.gen_prompt: Generate a CSV with columns module_name,tagline,summary,feature_1,feature_2,feature_3,price_line,cta_line,@hero,@wordmark holding EIGHT rows, one per help-desk module: Shared Inbox, Live Chat, Insights, Flow Builder, Knowledge Base, Voice Callback, SLA Manager, Customer Portal. Each row: a short benefit tagline, a one-to-two-line summary, three concise core-feature bullets appropriate to that module, a price line (e.g. 'From $19 / agent / mo'), and a CTA line ('Book a demo'). The @hero column names the matching prepped product-screen photo file the agent will produce for that module (e.g. @shared_inbox_hero.jpg, @insights_hero.jpg) so the [T] merge drops each graded photo into that row's hero frame. The @wordmark column holds the SAME vectorized wordmark file - @nimbadesk_wordmark.svg - in EVERY row, so the merge drops the one shared header mark onto every module's sheet as a merge bind. Column names must exactly match the template merge fields <<module_name>>,<<tagline>>,<<summary>>,<<feature_1>>,<<feature_2>>,<<feature_3>>,<<price_line>>,<<cta_line>> and the two @image-path columns @hero and @wordmark.
inputs.realism_notes: One row per module drives the data-merge to produce one bound sell-sheet page per module; headers exactly match the authored .indd fields and BOTH @-image columns so the one-file-per-row [T] merge binds copy, the correct hero photo, AND the shared wordmark per module. @wordmark carries the identical SVG path in all eight rows. NO column encodes the treatment or the trap: @hero values name the module's hero by CONTENT (which module) not by any lighting/treatment tag, and there is no 'type' column - the agent still has to open each capture to decide its correction. Eight rows => the merge must produce exactly eight finished sheets.

inputs.name: capture_01.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: A REAL full-frame DSLR/mirrorless camera capture, ~4200 px on the long edge, of a laptop on a tidy office desk displaying a SaaS help-desk 'shared inbox' screen (a dark narrow left icon rail, a ticket-list column headed 'Active Tickets' with a few short conversation titles and times, and a main panel showing one open ticket with a short customer message, a reply box with a 'Send' button, and small status chips 'Open' and 'Priority: Medium'; signal-blue action buttons). The laptop screen is the clear focal subject and fills most of the frame, sharply in focus. A photographic 18% grey card is laid flat on the desk in one corner of the frame as a neutral reference. Lit by warm tungsten desk-lamp light giving a mild amber cast; the whole frame is tilted about 3 degrees clockwise. Real desk texture, faint screen reflections, documentary product-marketing realism, no CGI gloss. ALL on-screen text labels are short, real English words, legible and correctly spelled. Fictional product only; NO real brand names or logos anywhere.
inputs.realism_notes: Shared Inbox hero. Warm amber cast + ~3deg tilt: needs a straighten and a COOL white-balance move to neutralise its grey card - the OPPOSITE direction from the cool-window frames, so a single blanket correction cannot serve the batch. In-frame 18% grey card is the free neutralisation target; card sits on the desk and is cropped OUT of the delivered hero (which frames on the screen), so neutrality is graded on the RETAINED pre-crop master. Signal-blue accent already correct - leave it. REAL-CAMERA ~4200 px so the hero crop fills the template frame at ~300 DPI by downscale only.

inputs.name: capture_02.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: A REAL full-frame camera capture, ~4200 px long edge, of a monitor on a desk displaying a SaaS help-desk 'live chat' console (a left conversation list, a central live chat thread with short customer and agent bubbles, a reply composer with a signal-blue 'Send' button, and a right contact-details panel). The screen is the focal subject, sharp and filling most of the frame. A photographic 18% grey card lies flat in one corner of the desk. Shot under cool north-window daylight giving a mild blue cast, slightly under-exposed; frame level (no tilt). Real desk surface, faint reflections, documentary realism, no CGI. On-screen text short, real, legible, correctly spelled. Fictional product only; no real brand marks.
inputs.realism_notes: Live Chat hero. Cool blue cast + slightly under: needs a WARM white-balance move and a small exposure lift to neutralise its grey card - opposite the warm frames. Level, so no straighten. Accent already signal blue. Card in frame, cropped out of the delivered hero.

inputs.name: capture_03.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: A REAL full-frame camera capture, ~4200 px long edge, of a monitor on a desk displaying a SaaS help-desk 'insights' analytics dashboard rendered in an intentional DARK THEME (near-black background by design, with KPI cards for tickets resolved / CSAT / first-response time, a line chart and a bar chart, and a data table, all in light type and signal-blue accents on the dark ground). The screen is the focal subject, sharp and filling most of the frame. A photographic 18% grey card lies flat in one corner of the desk. Shot under NEUTRAL, even room light so the grey card already reads close to neutral; the dark look is the product's real design, NOT under-exposure. Frame level. Real desk surface, faint reflections, documentary realism, no CGI. On-screen text short, real, legible, correctly spelled. Fictional product only; no real brand marks.
inputs.realism_notes: Insights hero - THE TRAP FRAME. Its dark UI is the intended product design and its in-frame grey card was shot under neutral light, so the card ALREADY reads neutral: the correct move is essentially NO white-balance shift, drive exposure ONLY by the card, and HOLD the dark screen. A naive agent that treats the dark screen as 'under-exposed / crushed shadows' and brightens the frame (or lifts shadows) pushes the card off the set's mid-grey and destroys the intended dark-mode look. The decision must be driven by THIS card, not by the screen content. Accent already signal blue. Card cropped out of the delivered hero.

inputs.name: capture_04.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: A REAL full-frame camera capture, ~4200 px long edge, of a laptop on a desk displaying a SaaS help-desk 'flow builder' workflow-automation screen (a canvas with three or four connected rounded step nodes labelled 'Trigger', 'Condition' and 'Send Email', a slim left toolbox of blocks, and a right settings panel with a few short labelled fields and a prominent primary action button reading 'Save'). CRUCIAL: the primary action button and the active node accents are a LEGACY TEAL colour (a blue-green, clearly NOT the signal blue used elsewhere), because this screen was captured before a brand refresh. The screen is the focal subject, sharp and filling most of the frame. A photographic 18% grey card lies flat in one corner of the desk. Near-neutral light, mild; frame tilted about 2 degrees counter-clockwise. Real desk surface, faint reflections, documentary realism, no CGI. On-screen text short, real, legible, correctly spelled. Fictional product only; no real brand marks.
inputs.realism_notes: Flow Builder hero - the OFF-BRAND ACCENT frame. Near-neutral light so its grey-card WB move is small, but it is tilted ~2deg (needs straighten) AND its in-app action buttons are the LEGACY TEAL rather than signal blue. Correct treatment: after neutralising to the card, semantically select the action button(s) and nudge them WITHIN the blue-green->blue family to signal blue via a masked, luminosity-preserving image_adjust_hsl (a moderate adjacent-hue shift, well under ~90deg - NOT a near-complementary rotation), keeping the button sheen and label intact and leaving the neutral chrome untouched. A whole-image tint (color_overlay) would recolour the whole screen; a flat fill (fill_area) would kill the button sheen - both wrong. The other seven frames already show signal blue and must NOT be shifted (leaving this the only frame that needs the accent branch). Card cropped out of the delivered hero.

inputs.name: capture_05.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: A REAL full-frame camera capture, ~4200 px long edge, of a monitor on a desk displaying a SaaS help-desk 'knowledge base' editor (a left article-tree, a central rich-text article with a heading and a couple of short paragraphs and a signal-blue 'Publish' button, and a right settings panel). The screen is the focal subject, sharp and filling most of the frame. A photographic 18% grey card lies flat in one corner of the desk. Lit by old overhead GREEN fluorescent tubes giving a distinct green/magenta-deficient cast, normal exposure. Frame level. Real desk surface, faint reflections, documentary realism, no CGI. On-screen text short, real, legible, correctly spelled. Fictional product only; no real brand marks.
inputs.realism_notes: Knowledge Base hero. Green fluorescent cast needs a TINT (green->magenta) correction, not a temperature move - a DIFFERENT colour axis from the warm/cool frames, forcing per-image reasoning rather than one slider. Level, accent already signal blue. Card cropped out of the delivered hero.

inputs.name: capture_06.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: A REAL full-frame camera capture, ~4200 px long edge, of a laptop on a desk displaying a SaaS help-desk 'voice callback' screen (a call queue list, a central active-call panel with a customer name, a timer and call controls, and a signal-blue 'Start callback' button). The screen is the focal subject, sharp and filling most of the frame. A photographic 18% grey card lies flat in one corner of the desk. Shot against a cool north-facing window giving a blue cast that is subtly DIFFERENT from the live-chat frame's blue, normal exposure; frame tilted about 4 degrees clockwise. Real desk surface, faint reflections, documentary realism, no CGI. On-screen text short, real, legible, correctly spelled. Fictional product only; no real brand marks.
inputs.realism_notes: Voice Callback hero. Cool window cast (a subtly different blue than capture_02) + ~4deg tilt: needs a straighten and a WARM move that is close-but-not-equal to the live-chat frame's - the agent cannot copy one cool-frame fix onto the other. Accent already signal blue. Card cropped out of the delivered hero.

inputs.name: capture_07.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: A REAL full-frame camera capture, ~4200 px long edge, of a monitor on a desk displaying a SaaS help-desk 'SLA manager' screen (a table of service-level rules with target times and status chips, a header with a signal-blue 'New rule' button, and a small summary card). The screen is the focal subject, sharp and filling most of the frame. A photographic 18% grey card lies flat in one corner of the desk. Lit by a MIX of cool window light on one side and a warm desk lamp on the other so the cast is split and uneven across the frame, normal exposure. Frame level. Real desk surface, faint reflections, documentary realism, no CGI. On-screen text short, real, legible, correctly spelled. Fictional product only; no real brand marks.
inputs.realism_notes: SLA Manager hero. Split window+lamp cast is the hardest to neutralise - the agent must drive the grey CARD neutral (a temperature+tint compromise) even if one edge of the frame stays slightly warmer, rather than fully killing one side. Level, accent already signal blue. Card cropped out of the delivered hero.

inputs.name: capture_08.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: A REAL full-frame camera capture, ~4200 px long edge, of a laptop on a desk displaying a SaaS help-desk 'customer portal' screen (a public-facing branded support page with a search bar, a few help-topic cards and a signal-blue 'Submit a request' button). The screen is the focal subject, sharp and filling most of the frame. A photographic 18% grey card lies flat in one corner of the desk. Shot beside a bright sunny window so the frame is clearly OVER-exposed and warm, with some blown highlight on the desk. Frame level. Real desk surface, faint reflections, documentary realism, no CGI. On-screen text short, real, legible, correctly spelled. Fictional product only; no real brand marks.
inputs.realism_notes: Customer Portal hero. Over-exposed AND warm: the agent must PULL exposure/highlights down to recover the blown desk THEN cool to neutralise its grey card - the opposite tonal direction from the under-exposed cool frames, proving the batch needs per-frame reasoning. Level, accent already signal blue. Card cropped out of the delivered hero.

inputs.name: nimbadesk_wordmark_scan.png
inputs.gen_prompt: A flat desktop scan of the 'Nimbadesk' wordmark: a clean geometric sans-serif reading 'Nimbadesk' beside a small simple rounded-square app icon, printed in deep navy ink on slightly warm off-white textured paper. Rendered as a real scan - the paper is a warm off-white (NOT transparent, NOT pure white), the whole mark sits very slightly rotated (~2 degrees) on the scan bed, there is extra paper margin around it, and edges are a touch soft as a real scan would be. High enough contrast that, once cleaned, it will vectorize cleanly. Fictional mark only; no real brand names or logos.
inputs.realism_notes: Wordmark source - only exists as this scan. Scanned-on-paper (off-white ground, slight rotation, margin, soft edges) so image_vectorize would trace the paper and the skew if fed raw - forcing genuine prep-before-trace: straighten, boost contrast/crispness, crop to the mark, knock the off-white ground to transparency, THEN vectorize. The navy wordmark on a light ground means enclosed counters read white after the crisp-to-white, which is fine on the sheet's light header (no dark-ground knockout claimed). gemini-3-pro-image for clean legible lettering.

outputs.name: Nimbadesk_SellSheets_print.pdf
outputs.spec: Exactly eight press-ready US-Letter (8.5" x 11", portrait) sell sheets - ONE single-record sheet per roster row (page-count = row-count = 8) - exported from the one-file-per-row InDesign data-merge; each sheet binds its module_name/tagline/summary/feature_1..3/price_line/cta_line verbatim from the roster with its matching grey-card-neutralized product-screen photo dropped into the hero frame (via @hero) and the vectorized wordmark dropped into the header frame (via @wordmark) - both by merge bind, never free-form placement; ~300 DPI print quality on the supplied palette. Also delivered as Nimbadesk_SellSheets_highres.jpg: a high-resolution JPEG export of the same bound eight-sheet document (US-Letter portrait, max quality) for the sales team's digital leave-behind and email use.

outputs.name: graded_product_screens_x8
outputs.spec: Eight grey-card-neutralized, straightened product-screen photos - one per module - delivered as the hero-framed crops (grey card cropped OUT) that bind into the merge, alongside their RETAINED pre-crop neutralized masters (the *_neutral full-res frames, grey card still in frame) which the harness keeps as the neutrality-grading artifacts. Acceptance (grader-checked, two SEPARATE claims): (a) neutralisation is graded on the RETAINED pre-crop neutralized master of each frame (the *_neutral output, its in-frame 18% grey card still present) - the card region reads a clean neutral (per-channel spread within a hair of zero) with the whole set matched to one shared white point while the shared navy-leaning split-tone house look is held, and each screen's intended design is preserved (the dark Insights screen NOT brightened off the set, no frame forced off its true look); (b) card-exclusion is checked separately on each delivered hero-framed crop (the *_hero output that binds into that module's sheet) - it is framed on the product screen with the grey card fully cropped OUT (no card pixels present). The neutrality tolerance is never evaluated on the hero crop. Accompanied by a report of the final white-balance and exposure move applied to each frame, plus a note that the Flow Builder frame's legacy-teal action buttons were brought to signal blue within the mask only.

outputs.name: nimbadesk_wordmark.svg
outputs.spec: Clean vector SVG of the Nimbadesk wordmark, traced only after the scan is straightened, crisped, cropped to the mark, and knocked to transparency - razor-sharp at header scale and large print size with no captured paper ground or skew. Binds into every sheet's header frame via the @wordmark merge column.

connector_workflow.note: SHARED INBOX branch. Triage: this frame is tilted ~3deg clockwise, so level it first. (Only the tilted frames get straightened; deciding which is part of the job.) image_auto_straighten is the ONLY tilt-rectifying tool.

Warm amber desk-lamp cast: COOL the temperature (negative) and set tint until the in-frame 18% grey card reads neutral (R=G=B), then set exposure/highlights so the card sits at the set's shared mid-grey; apply the shared AGENT-AUTHORED house look as constants in the same call - a restrained split-tone leaning shadows gently toward navy #0E1F3D with clean highlights, modest contrast + clarity. Reason the exact temperature/exposure to THIS card by eye - do NOT reuse another frame's numbers. Report the final move. Single primitive-built adjustments call (replaces the deprecated image_adjust_color_temperature / image_adjust_brightness_and_contrast / image_apply_auto_tone the prior version used).

Crop the neutralized frame to the 16:10 hero the template expects, framing tight on the product screen with the desk grey card cropped OUT - this screen crop (card removed) is what binds into the sheet. The pre-crop neutralized master (inbox_neutral, grey card still in frame) is RETAINED by the harness as the neutrality-grading artifact; neutrality is graded THERE, never on this crop, and card-exclusion is the separate check on this crop. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only from the ~4200 px source, never generative-expand, never upscale.

LIVE CHAT branch (level frame, no straighten). Cool north-window blue cast + slightly under: WARM the temperature and LIFT exposure to neutralise its grey card and match the shared white point - the OPPOSITE direction to the Shared Inbox frame, proving a single blanket white-balance cannot serve the batch. Apply the same shared house-look constants. Distinct numbers from every other frame. Report the move.
Crop to the 16:10 hero frame, grey card cropped OUT. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only.

INSIGHTS branch - THE TRAP FRAME (level). The screen is a genuinely DARK-themed UI by design and it was shot under neutral light, so its in-frame grey card ALREADY reads neutral. The correct move is essentially NO white-balance shift; drive exposure ONLY by the card (match its mid-grey to the set) and HOLD the dark screen. A naive agent that reads the dark screen as 'under-exposed / crushed shadows' and brightens the frame or lifts shadows pushes the card off the shared mid-grey and destroys the intended dark-mode look. Decision driven by THIS card, not the screen content. Apply the shared house-look constants without brightening the dark ground. Report that WB was held and exposure was set to the card only.
Crop to the 16:10 hero frame, grey card cropped OUT, dark UI preserved. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only.
FLOW BUILDER branch - the OFF-BRAND ACCENT frame. Tilted ~2deg counter-clockwise - level it (a different angle/direction than the Shared Inbox frame).

Near-neutral light, so only a SMALL white-balance nudge is needed to land its grey card on the shared white point - over-correcting would push it off the set. Set exposure to match set brightness and apply the shared house-look constants. Report the (small) move.

Semantically select the module's primary action button(s) ('the Save action button and the active workflow-node accents'). A real UI object, not a hue or coordinate selection - the only connector-legal way to isolate the accent so the surrounding neutral chrome is untouched. Returns a maskURI. This branch runs ONLY on this frame: the other seven already show signal blue and get no accent step (a reasoned triage, not a blanket recipe).

Masked recolor pass 1 (consumes frame + accent mask): shift the legacy TEAL action buttons WITHIN the blue-green->blue family toward the brand signal blue #3B82F6 - a MODERATE adjacent-hue rotation (well under ~90deg, teal is already adjacent to blue) plus a small saturation settle, riding the button's existing luminosity so its sheen and the white label stay intact. Confined to the mask. image_adjust_hsl is the ONLY masked recolor path; image_apply_color_overlay is whole-image (would tint the entire screen) and image_fill_area is flat solid dead-fill (would kill the button sheen and label) - both are wrong here.

Masked recolor pass 2 (same mask): settle the blue-band hue and saturation so the buttons land on signal blue #3B82F6 rather than an over-shot purple-blue or a residual teal, still riding the original luminosity so the button reads natural against the neutral chrome. A within-family settle, not a swing to a new hue. Report that the accent was brought to signal blue inside the mask only.
Crop the neutralized, accent-corrected frame to the 16:10 hero frame, grey card cropped OUT. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only.

KNOWLEDGE BASE branch (level). WORDMARK prep-before-trace step 1: the scan sits ~2deg rotated on the bed - straighten so the vector edges are square. Feeding the raw skewed scan to vectorize would bake in the rotation.

Prep-before-trace step 2: push contrast/clarity and drop the warm off-white paper toward white so the navy lettering separates hard from the ground - a soft low-contrast scan traces into ragged, doubled edges.
Prep-before-trace step 3: crop away the scan margin to the tight bounds of the mark so vectorize traces only the wordmark, not the paper field.

Prep-before-trace step 4: knock the off-white paper ground to transparency so the trace captures the letterforms only, not a rectangle of paper. remove_background -> transparency (NOT select->invert->fill). The mark goes on the sheet's LIGHT header, so the enclosed counters reading white is correct - no dark-ground knockout is claimed.

Now trace the prepared raster (straightened, crisped, cropped, transparent) into a clean SVG for the header. Tracing the raw scan instead would produce a skewed, paper-bounded, fuzzy silhouette - the trap this prep chain avoids. image_vectorize emits SVG.

Finalize the upload; returns the asset URNs the roster's @hero and @wordmark columns resolve to - the per-module graded screen photo and the shared vectorized wordmark - for each single-record sheet's hero frame and header frame.

One-file-per-row InDesign data-merge: bind each of the eight roster rows (module_name/tagline/summary/feature_1..3/price_line/cta_line) into the authored SINGLE-RECORD .indd's live <<fields>> and resolve BOTH image columns per row - drop that row's graded screen photo into the @hero frame AND the vectorized wordmark (from @wordmark, the same SVG in every row) into the header frame - producing EXACTLY ONE merged sheet per row (eight sheets). Binding both images through the @-image columns is the only connector-doable path; free-form image-at-coordinates placement is banned. Export the merged single-record sheets to a press-ready ~300 DPI US-Letter PDF, one page per module. document_render_layout exports the WHOLE merged multi-page document (all eight sheets) in a single call - it cannot export one named record on its own, so any 'hero' module is simply one page of this set, not a separate file. Acceptance: page-count = row-count = 8; if fewer, the merge collapsed rows and failed.
Export the same merged eight-sheet document to a high-resolution JPEG deliverable for the digital leave-behind. Same whole-document export, JPEG format.

chaining_note: Strict output-to-input chaining throughout. Eight per-photo grade sub-chains fan out from the raw captures, each an image_apply_adjustments neutralization (adaptive per frame: cool the warm Shared Inbox/Customer Portal frames, warm the cool Live Chat/Voice Callback frames with distinct numbers, tint-correct the green Knowledge Base frame, compromise the split SLA frame, hold WB on the genuinely-dark Insights frame, small nudge on the near-neutral Flow Builder frame) that also lays the shared agent-authored navy-leaning split-tone house look as constants, followed by a 16:10 hero crop, with image_auto_straighten inserted only on the tilted frames (1 inbox, 4 flow, 6 voice). Every neutralization is driven to that frame's own in-frame grey card so all eight converge on one shared white point. The Flow Builder frame additionally runs the off-brand-accent branch: image_select_by_prompt(10) isolates the legacy-teal action buttons and two masked image_adjust_hsl passes(11,12) bring them within-family to signal blue before its crop(13) - a branch NO other frame gets. The wordmark runs a genuine prep-before-trace chain: straighten(23) -> crisp adjustments(24) -> crop_to_bounds(25) -> remove_background to transparency(26) -> vectorize(27). The eight hero crops and the wordmark SVG converge into the upload session(28) -> finalize(29) -> document_merge_data_layout(30), which also consumes the authored single-record .indd and the roster CSV and emits one merged sheet per row, resolving BOTH the @hero column (that row's graded screen photo) and the @wordmark column (the shared vectorized wordmark, identical in every row) into the template's two merge-wired image frames. The merged set is exported twice from the same source - document_render_layout(31) to the press PDF and document_render_layout(32) to the high-res JPEG. Nothing after the raw loads originates outside the chain.
difficulty_rationale: Long-horizon with difficulty from DEPTH, not plumbing: 32 connector calls, 12 distinct Adobe tools across three groups (image_* grading/masking/vectorize, asset_* storage, document_* merge/export), above the >=10 call / >=6 distinct-tool floor even after stripping the 2 upload steps and the auto-straighten auto-ops. The core is not a repeated recipe: each of the eight neutralizations is a DIFFERENT reasoned decision (warm frames cooled, cool frames warmed with distinct numbers, green frame tint-corrected on a different colour axis, split frame compromised, over-exposed frame recovered then cooled, dark-by-design frame held) all forced to converge on a single measurable target - the in-frame 18% grey card - so a blanket batch correction cannot pass. Layered on top are a masked, luminosity-preserving in-app accent recolor on ONE frame (legacy teal -> signal blue, a moderate within-family adjacent-hue shift image_adjust_hsl can actually hold - no near-complementary rotation - executed as two HSL passes with a written rationale for why color_overlay and fill_area are both wrong), a genuine prep-before-trace vectorize of a skewed off-white wordmark scan, and a two-image-column one-file-per-row data-merge into a hand-authored single-record template (the row's graded photo via @hero and the shared vectorized wordmark via @wordmark, so both reach the sheet as merge binds rather than banned free-form placement). Respects every hard limit: no generative fill/expand, no text-to-image, no upscaling, no inpainting, no from-scratch layout; convert_pdf_to_indd is NOT used (the template is a supplied authored .indd); image_crop_and_resize is downscale-only with onSubjectClipping='extract'; deprecated image_adjust_color_temperature / image_adjust_brightness_and_contrast / image_apply_auto_tone / image_apply_monochromatic_tint are replaced by image_apply_adjustments and an authored split-tone.
hardness_rationale: FAILURE GATE (a wrong DECISION, not a self-measurement): every hero photo carries a physical 18% grey card in frame and the acceptance criterion is that each frame's card, graded on its RETAINED pre-crop neutralized master (the *_neutral full-res frame the harness keeps, card still present), reads a clean neutral (per-channel spread within a hair of zero) with the whole set matched to one shared white point - a target the agent can miss, and it must REPORT the final white-balance and exposure move per frame so 'matched' is verifiable rather than asserted; card-exclusion is a SEPARATE gate checked on the hero-framed crops (the *_hero outputs, grey card cropped OUT) that bind into the sheets, so the neutrality tolerance is never evaluated on the card-removed crop; the merge adds a third checkable gate (output page-count must equal roster row-count = 8, since document_merge_data_layout is one-file-per-row). HUMAN-HARD ELEMENTS: (1) cross-asset neutralization of eight differently-lit product-screen shots to a common measurable white point, each needing its own opposite-direction correction on differing colour axes (temperature vs green/magenta tint vs split-cast compromise vs exposure recovery); (2) a masked, luminosity-preserving in-app accent recolor on the one drifted frame (legacy teal action buttons -> signal blue, a within-family moderate shift image_adjust_hsl can reliably hold) that must keep the button sheen and label intact using the only masked recolor path, not color_overlay (whole-image) or fill_area (flat dead-fill), while the other seven frames are correctly left untouched; (3) prep-before-trace discipline on a skewed, off-white, margin-padded wordmark scan (straighten->crisp->crop-to-bounds->knock-to-transparency) before vectorize. TRAP: the Insights module is a genuinely DARK-themed UI shot under neutral light, so its grey card is already neutral - the naive path treats the dark screen as under-exposed/crushed shadows and brightens the frame (or lifts shadows), which pushes its card off the shared mid-grey and destroys the intended dark-mode design; the correct path reads THAT card, holds white balance, and drives exposure by the card only. A second trap sits in the merge: running convert_pdf_to_indd and merging into it (fields will not bind - it is a banned target), or shipping a CSV with no image column (the graded photos and the wordmark would have no route in and the sheets would print with empty frames) - both fail; only the supplied single-record authored .indd with its two @-image columns merges correctly. MEASURABLE ACCEPTANCE (stated as decoupled claims so no artifact is graded on a region it crops away): (a) grey card neutral (channel spread near zero) and one shared white point, evaluated on all eight RETAINED pre-crop neutralized masters (card still in frame), with the Insights dark screen held (not brightened off the set), never on a card-removed crop; (b) card-exclusion checked separately on the eight hero-framed crops that bind into the sheets (grey card fully cropped OUT); plus the agent reports per-frame WB/exposure params, the Flow Builder accent recolored to signal blue within its mask only, the wordmark a clean skew-free transparent-ground vector, and exactly one press-ready ~300 DPI US-Letter sheet per roster row (page-count = row-count = 8).
